Subject: Dedicated capacity / surge for model fleet

Hi Monica,

Quick context: Crestfall is piloting a live robotics orchestration assistant that spikes during batch test windows and firmware rollout validations. We expect normal steady-state traffic ~150 rps for small models and heavy spikes to ~1.2k rps for ~30-60 minute windows, a few times per week.

Can Redwood's Dedicated offering give us a predictable commit with a defined surge window and an autoscale policy that won't exhaust our budget during proofs? We're looking for:
- A recommended reserve slab for steady load
- An approach for controlled temporary headroom for burst windows
- Rough cost estimate for the surge allowance (monthly)

Attached is a small telemetry sample and our load projection. Happy to join a call.

Thanks,
Daniel

Crestfall Robotics

Thanks Daniel — this is helpful. Quick answers up front and then a proposal:

Short answer: yes. We recommend a tiered slab + transient burst pool with enforced eviction and preemptive fallbacks to smaller model variants to guard cost and SLOs.

Proposed next steps:
1) We size a steady-state reserved slab for your baseline (targeting 150 rps equivalent).
2) We allocate a shared transient headroom pool for scheduled spikes and configure a per-deal burst cap (in GPU-hours).
3) We define an autoscale policy with:
   - warm spare instances (KV cache primed)
   - burst admission controls (token-based gating)
   - automatic model-fallback and per-request routing policy for degraded capacity.

I've attached a first-pass capacity model and a PDF with a tiered surge proposal. Karthik and Rishi can dig into the kernel/memory implications.

Can we schedule 30 min tomorrow to walk the numbers?

Best,

Daniel, Monica — digging into the telemetry and the XLS: a couple quick technical observations we should account for when translating rps to GPU capacity:

- Model mix matters: your heavy traffic includes a large proportion of a 3B-parameter model that favors attention memory and KV cache; those require more warm-GPU memory than a 7B FP16-quantized endpoint.
- Spike shape: 1.2k rps sustained for 30–60 mins implies that burst pool needs both headroom and warm-up capacity. Cold spins will blow latency SLOs.
- Suggested architecture:
  * Reserve slab sized for 150 rps steady-state (estimate: 4x A100-80GB equivalence for KV residency given your model mix)
  * A transient burst pool of 6 A100-80GB-equivalent units (time-limited) that sits idle but with warmed caches during scheduled windows
  * Pre-warm hooks + a 3-minute admission ramp with token gating to smooth arrival spikes

I'll inline a compact cost delta in the proposal; Rishi, can you validate the eviction and fallback thresholds?

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <dpark@crestfall.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity / surge for model fleet

Confirmed on thresholds. A couple of policy items to surface for procurement and SRE alignment: 

- Eviction order: ephemeral batch jobs -> low-priority model variants -> longtail background tasks. No customer inference requests will be evicted without automatic fallback to a smaller model variant.
- Billing unit for burst: bill by committed GPU-hours consumed above the reserve slab, with per-minute granularity and a monthly cap to avoid runaway cost.
- Safety guard: if burst pool consumption exceeds X% of monthly allowance, automatic routing splits to hosted API compatible endpoints (fallback) and an on-call alert to Crestfall ops.

I'll attach a draft autoscale policy doc for review. This encodes the warm-spare behavior plus admission control.

Attachment: draft_autoscale_policy_crestfall.docx

—Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood proposal: tiered surge allocation (pricing & SLA)

Hi procurement team / Daniel — looping procurement per your request. Attached is the formal proposal and a simple monthly pricing model for:

- Reserve slab: 4x A100-80GB-equivalent dedicated — covers baseline (150 rps)
- Burst allowance: 6x A100-80GB-equivalent shared transient pool, metered in GPU-hours
- Pricing model: reserve = fixed monthly commit; burst = metered at $X per GPU-hour with a monthly cap (we recommend initial cap = 450 GPU-hours/month).
- SLA addendum: during scheduled windows we support a 99.9% latency target for primary endpoints; fallback endpoints will have a looser SLO and are explicitly called out.

Action items for Crestfall to approve:
1) Approve the reserve slab and initial burst cap.
2) Sign the attachment MSA & the surge annex (DocuSign link below).
3) Confirm scheduled spike cadence so we can enable pre-warm hooks.

Monica — thanks for the clear framing. Procurement reviewed the numbers and the MSA; two quick notes before DocuSign: 

1) We can accept the reserve slab and burst construct provided the monthly cap is adjustable after the first 30 days.
2) We want one change in the safety guard: add a human approval step if burst consumption would automatically route >50% of traffic to hosted fallback for more than 15 consecutive minutes. We still want automatic split, but with an ops gating step.

Assuming those two items are incorporated we can sign and schedule our weekly maintenance windows for pre-warm. Please update the DocuSign and we will route for signature.

Thanks,
Daniel
Head of Platform, Crestfall Robotics
